title: The Grunion Run, xvi
logline: Sixteenth year. The Friday of the ring week. Chloe at the run, the ring still a dot in the lantern light. The strip holds out one more night. The dog stays home.

panels.composition: The beach, lanterns, the run. GULLY's thermos line. WOOD and CHLOE at the surf, not touching. Her left hand in her coat pocket. No dog.

image.prompt: a night beach festival with lanterns, a man with a thermos, a thin man and a woman standing at a surf line of silver fish not touching, her left hand in her coat pocket, razor-sharp ink with a muted wash

panels.composition: Her hand out of the pocket, pointing at a fish. On it: a dot. Lantern light on the dot. The strip refuses to enlarge it.

image.prompt: close-up of a woman's hand pointing at a silver fish on wet sand with a tiny dot of light on one finger
image.notes: The ring is a dot. Friday. Tomorrow it's drawn right (dw_2013-03-16).

panels.composition: Chloe, looking at him looking at her hand.

balloons.text: I see a lot of fish.

image.prompt: a woman looking at a man who is looking at her hand, both lit by lanterns

panels.composition: Silent. The surf, the fish, the lanterns. The two of them. Where the dog was every year: sand. The first Grunion Run without him. The dot.
props: empty sand where the dog stood

image.prompt: silent wide night beach panel with silver fish and lanterns, a man and a woman at the surf, an empty patch of sand beside them, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'I see a lot of fish.' The dot, one more night. No dog.
